name: Step-by-Step Encounter Building
summary: Building a combat encounter runs in six steps: think about the encounter's premise, choose its difficulty, determine the party's encounter strength, determine the encounter…
description: Building a combat encounter runs in six steps: think about the encounter's premise, choose its difficulty, determine the party's encounter strength, determine the encounter budget, spend that budget on creatures, and build initiative groups. The guidelines are explicitly not a science — the heroes the players create, the map, the treasures they carry, the dice, and each player's tactical acumen all move the result, so expect to adjust the guidelines to your group.

description: Extreme encounters feature threats the heroes are unlikely to survive if they fight to the bitter end. name: Encounter Strength
summary: A party's encounter strength (ES) is the benchmark you buy monsters against.
description: A party's encounter strength (ES) is the benchmark you buy monsters against. Each hero's encounter strength starts at a baseline of 4, plus 2 for each level of the hero — a 3rd-level hero has an encounter strength of 10. Add every hero's encounter strength together for the party's ES, so five 3rd-level heroes have an ES of 50. Each retainer or other NPC fighting alongside the heroes counts as a hero of their own level.

properties.party_formula: sum of every hero's encounter strength

source: Draw Steel Monsters Book, ch. 1 (Monster Basics) (mcdm.monsters.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Factoring Victories into Encounter Strength
summary: Victories make heroes more powerful on the way to their next level.
description: Victories make heroes more powerful on the way to their next level. For every 2 Victories the heroes have earned on average, increase the party's encounter strength as if there were another hero in the party — a party of 3rd-level heroes with 2 or 3 Victories each gains 10 ES, and with 6 Victories each gains 30. Be careful that the larger encounter strength does not push you past the recommended number of creatures: it is usually better to use higher-cost creatures than to add extra ones.

properties.formula: add one hero of the party's level per 2 average Victories
properties.caution: prefer higher-EV creatures over more creatures

name: Spending the Encounter Budget
summary: You spend your encounter budget to buy hostile creatures.
description: You spend your encounter budget to buy hostile creatures. Each creature costs a number of budget points equal to its encounter value (EV). Choose a variety of creature roles for a more dynamic fight. Dynamic terrain objects are bought out of the same budget.

name: Choosing Creature Levels
summary: Choose creatures whose level is no more than 2 greater than the heroes' level — for a party of 5th-level heroes, creatures of level 7 and below.
description: Choose creatures whose level is no more than 2 greater than the heroes' level — for a party of 5th-level heroes, creatures of level 7 and below. If the heroes have 6 or more Victories you can push that to within 3 levels. Solo creatures are the exception: restrict them to no more than 1 level above the party's average, because a solo's abilities dish out a lot of damage for their level. This level comparison is the only role level plays in encounter building; everything else relies on encounter value and organization.

summary: Whenever you spend EV on minions, you buy them four at a time, and it is recommended to buy at least two sets for any encounter because minions are not effective in smaller numbers.
description: Whenever you spend EV on minions, you buy them four at a time, and it is recommended to buy at least two sets for any encounter because minions are not effective in smaller numbers. The minions you buy can then be arranged into squads of any size up to a maximum of eight. More minions in a squad makes each minion turn more effective; more squads is easier to track.

name: Number of Creatures and Stat Blocks
summary: Too many creatures, or too many different stat blocks, turns an exciting combat into a slog.
description: Too many creatures, or too many different stat blocks, turns an exciting combat into a slog. In general do not use more than eight creatures per hero at a time. If the encounter has more than three creatures per hero, at least half of them should be minions. Typically use no more than six different kinds of stat blocks in an encounter, though you can manage more if many of them are simple minion stat blocks.

name: Building Initiative Groups
summary: Put the encounter's foes into initiative groups, with every creature in a group acting on the same turn.
description: Put the encounter's foes into initiative groups, with every creature in a group acting on the same turn. Try to keep each group's total EV between the encounter strength of one and two heroes, so the group can hold its own against any one hero without overwhelming them. A group worth less than that is fine; a group worth more is fine when it is a single creature or the heroes have racked up a lot of Victories. In a battle without a solo creature, aim for about as many initiative groups as there are heroes, plus or minus one or two.

name: Quick Encounter Building
summary: A faster method that skips the EV arithmetic.
description: A faster method that skips the EV arithmetic. Note the party's level and size, then add one hero to the party for every two Victories the heroes have on average. The encounter has a number of hero slots equal to that adjusted party size. Fill each slot with creatures at the listed rates, adjusting the slot count and the creature levels by difficulty. Then include one or two dynamic terrain objects for standard-or-easier encounters and two or three for hard and extreme ones, using only objects of the heroes' level or lower.

name: Parties Large and Small
summary: Draw Steel was made and tested for groups of three to six heroes including retainers.
description: Draw Steel was made and tested for groups of three to six heroes including retainers. For a party of seven or more, solo creatures no longer live up to the name — give them lackeys or extra dynamic terrain objects. For a party of three or fewer, consider giving the heroes retainers, because small parties struggle against solo creatures and large groups of minions.
source: Draw Steel Monsters Book, ch. 1 (Monster Basics) (mcdm.monsters.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: How Many Fights Before a Respite
summary: A group of heroes can generally handle from 4 to 6 Victories' worth of combat encounters before needing a respite to refresh their Stamina and Recoveries.
description: A group of heroes can generally handle from 4 to 6 Victories' worth of combat encounters before needing a respite to refresh their Stamina and Recoveries. Like encounter building itself this is not exact — treasures, dice, encounter composition, and downtime projects all move the number.
